items.title: Ben Simmons sparks 76ers rumors with LeBron James photo hint
items.content:
Ben Simmons 76ersAfter being run out of town five years ago, Ben Simmons posted on social media that he’s currently lacing up The King’s boots.

The former No. 1 overall pick in the 2016 NBA Draft had such a bad time in Philadelphia that he had to be sent out in a trade and was even kicked out of practice at one point, but is now posting pictures of LeBron James basketball sneakers after the all-time great signed with his former team.

Simmons said in June he “maybe [will] go back to Philly” in an attempt to reignite his basketball career despite flaming out of the league and beginning a professional fishing career.

Ben Simmons posts on social media some new LeBron James basketball shoes that he’s purchased.  Instagram Ben SimmonsThough those June comments are when James to the 76ers looked like a non-possibility. 

With James now in the fold, the 76ers are among the NBA Finals favorites, as the team has also added Jaylen Brown to complement other high-end talent.

Simmons had a phenomenal start to his career in Philadelphia, averaging at least 15.8 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.7 assists per game in each of his first three seasons while also being named first-team All-Defense twice in that span.

Ben Simmons is flirting with the 76ers ore blatantly than ever.  NBAE via Getty ImagesHowever, in year four, he had a nightmare playoff series against the Heat that apparently caused serious harm to his career.

Simmons, 30, forced a trade out of Philadelphia and had a bizarre mental block that ended with him often passing on open layups when he was traded to the Brooklyn Nets for James Harden.

Los Angeles Lakers’ LeBron James and Philadelphia 76ers’ Joel Embiid are now teammates. AP Photo/Matt SlocumAnother potential destination if he did return to the NBA would be in Miami.

“Miami would be nice. And not because it’s Miami,” Simmons said. “I like Erik Spoelstra, I like the Heat, I like their organization, I like the culture.”

items.title: LeBron James can help Tyrese Maxey be better than ever
items.content:
PHILADELPHIA, PA - FEBRUARY 26: Tyrese Maxey #0 of the Philadelphia 76ers reacts to becoming the Philadelphia 76ers franchise leader in 3-pointer field goals made during the game against the Miami Heat on February 26, 2026 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	LeBron James is a Philadelphia 76er. I know you’ll have read that a lot by now, but I don’t think another mention hurts when it still feels this surreal.

There’s so much to think about with LeBron’s arrival. Beyond the excitement that the possible greatest player of all time chose Philly for his final ring chase, signing on the absurd value of a minimum contract, there are all the basketball nuances to consider. How much will he even need to score on a team with Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, and another rising star in VJ Edgecombe? How will LeBron perform defensively as the new power forward? How will Nick Nurse stagger the team’s stacked array of stars and scoring talent?

There’s lots to think about and look forward to. 

For now, though, let’s focus on LeBron’s new All-NBA teammate, Tyrese Maxey. Because their relationship on the court has the potential to be the most entertaining and dynamic of any new combination LeBron will form on the team.

We all know Maxey has blossomed into a stellar, high-volume scorer. He just set a new career-high with 28.3 points per game on a 58.8 true shooting percentage last season (his most efficient season in three years) as he made the All-NBA Third Team for the first time. At every level of the floor, Maxey’s versatility and efficiency as a scorer has reached elite levels. He can burn opponents not only with his speed and acrobatic finishing, but his smooth dribbling and pull-up shooting. And along with his scoring talent, his passing has steadily improved over the course of his career as well. He’s a sharper playmaker and pick-and-roll leader who takes great care of the ball, and just averaged a career-high 6.6 assists to only 2.4 turnovers per game.

However, Maxey has always thrived most when he’s able to spend a healthy amount of time doing what he does best: being one of the top off-ball scorers in the NBA.

He’s always excelled as a frenetic attacker off the catch with how he can burst downhill against closeouts and scrambling defenses, and his shooting off movement and running off screens has only improved throughout his career. He can hit threes on the catch and around screens at speed, at tough angles, and from well beyond the arc. Apart from a down spell in 2024-25 with three-point shooting, Maxey has routinely shot lights out on catch-and-shoot threes for years:

items.title: Dillon Mitchell signs two-way deal with Boston Celtics, dashing hopes of St. John’s men’s basketball return
items.content:
NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MARCH 14: Dillon Mitchell #1 of the St. John's Red Storm dribbles during the second half of the 2026 Big East Men's Tournament Championship game against the Connecticut Huskies at Madison Square Garden on March 14, 2026 in New York City. The Red Storm won 72-52. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images	The dream that star St. John’s forward Dillon Mitchell would turn down an NBA contract and return to the Red Storm for his fifth season of college basketball was only that: a dream.

The Boston Celtics shut the door on rumors that Mitchell would come back to college and use his extra year of eligibility granted by a Colorado federal judge, announcing that it has signed its 40th overall selection in the 2026 NBA draft to a two-way contract, voiding the former Red Storm standout’s remaining amateur eligibility. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

We have signed Dillon Mitchell to a two-way contract ☘️ pic.twitter.com/TPL8qezhum

— Boston Celtics (@celtics) August 5, 2026Mitchell becomes the second former St. John’s star selected in this year’s NBA draft to sign a professional contract. Zuby Ejiofor inked a four-year rookie-scale contract worth $17.3 million with the Atlanta Hawks not long after he was drafted with the 23rd overall pick. Bryce Hopkins has yet to sign a contract with the Denver Nuggets after getting drafted with the 49th overall pick, but wouldn’t have been eligible to return to college anyway after his five-year eligibility clock expired.

The Celtics rookie stood out amongst his peers during the NBA Summer League, averaging 13.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 2.7 steals, and 1.3 blocks while shooting 47.2 percent from the field and even tripling his senior year three-point output, firing 3-of-8 from long range across three games.

Mitchell can earn only $678,882 on a two-way contract, half the value of a guaranteed rookie minimum deal, and is limited to playing up to 50 NBA games. This means Mitchell is most likely splitting time with the Boston Celtics and developing with their G-League affiliate, the Maine Celtics.

In his only season with the Red Storm, the former McDonald’s All-American posted 8.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.3 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game on 55.9% shooting from the field, securing positions on the All-Big East Third Team and Big East All-Defensive Team.

As Mitchell is now off the board and St. John’s still has one remaining roster spot to fill, the Red Storm will focus on finding a starting-caliber replacement for stellar Syracuse transfer Donnie Freeman at power forward.

The Red Storm are reportedly one of the many teams eyeing All-SEC forward Keyshawn Hall. The well-traveled 6-foot-7 swingman never spent more than one season playing for a single team, hopping between UNLV, George Mason, UCF, and Auburn. items.title: International Notes: McClung, Ryan, Jokic, Bertans
items.content:
Mac McClung, a three-time slam dunk contest champion and two-time G League MVP, has signed a one-year deal with Basket Girona in the Spanish ACB, the team announced in a press release. It will be McClung’s first time playing overseas.

For all his success at the G League level, McClung hasn’t been able to find a long-term NBA home since leaving Texas Tech in 2021, appearing in 17 total games with five teams over the past five years. He got into three games with Indiana early last season before being waived on November 7, then signed a two-way contract with Chicago in February and saw time in eight more contests.

“His main characteristic is his scoring ability,” said Fernando San Emeterio, sporting director for Basket Girona. “He has been a scorer throughout his career. He is capable of generating his own shots and scoring from the paint, from mid-range and also from the three-point line. Another of the qualities that we like a lot is his ability to generate play for his teammates. Based on the attention he arouses in defenses and his ability to break them, he is a very good passer. Now the challenge is to transfer all this potential to European basketball, since he has never played there yet. … We believe that it fits perfectly with our style of play and our identity. In addition, he is a very competitive player, and we are delighted to be able to count on him.”

There’s more international news to pass along:

Former NBA forward Matt Ryan has signed with Maxima Roma for the upcoming season, per Geoff Gillingham of Euroleague.net. Ryan, who spent time with five NBA teams from 2021-25, played with Dubai Basketball last season.
Nuggets center Nikola Jokic is part of the 18-man Serbian squad that will compete in the FIBA World Cup Qualifiers this month, according to Eurohoops. The team will play exhibition games against France on August 20 and 23 before hosting Iceland on August 28 and traveling to Italy three days later.
Davis Bertans is retiring from international competition after representing Latvia for the past 15 years, relays Dario Skerletic of Sportando. Bertans, who plays for Dubai Basketball, made the announcement in an online post. “I sincerely hope that Latvian basketball is in a much better place today than it was when I played my first game for the national team,” he wrote. “From now on, I will be one of its biggest supporters. I will always cheer for the team and, whenever I have the chance, I’ll be in the stands supporting the guys.”

items.title: The 5 most interesting potential 2027 NBA free agents, including a perennial All-Star on the Warriors
items.content:
With the bulk of the 2026 NBA offseason’s player movement now concluded, and with the calendar now flipped to August, it’s time to start looking ahead to what’s coming next in the NBA, both this season and afterward.

In that spirit, and in the interest of killing some time in the depths of the summer, let’s take a look at the five most interesting players — to me! — who could wind up on the open market next summer.

For the purposes of this exercise, I’m excluding players that I expect to sign extensions with their franchises when they become eligible to do so before hitting free agency (like Stephen Curry in Golden State later this month or Giannis Antetokounmpo in Miami in February) or whenever they decide it’s most contractually advantageous for them (like Nikola Jokić in Denver) and players whose whole deal currently feels up-in-the-air enough to make projecting what might be coming next for them something of a fool’s errand (like Kawhi Leonard in Los Angeles, Toronto or Parts Unknown).

We begin with the other perennial All-Star and All-NBA performer in the Bay Area:

Jimmy Butler, WarriorsWhen the Golden State Warriors open the 2026-27 NBA season, Butler will be 37 years old, with one season and $56.8 million remaining on the two-year extension that he signed with the Warriors after they dealt for him at the 2025 trade deadline. He will also most likely be in street clothes, continuing to rehabilitate his surgically repaired right knee; while he’s reportedly “turned the corner” in the process of coming back from a torn anterior cruciate ligament in January, we probably won’t see Jimmy back on the court until midseason at the earliest.

That would leave about half a season for a Warriors team that floundered after his injury, and that has essentially seemed to be killing time this summer, to make a case that there’s still something worth investing in when it comes to the graybeard core of Curry, Butler and Draymond Green. Since Butler’s arrival in February of 2025, the Warriors have gone 45-20 in games in which that trio has suited up — a 57-win pace across portions of two regular seasons and one postseason, which included a seven-game victory over a dogged Rockets squad in 2025’s opening round before Curry suffered a hamstring injury in Game 1 of the conference semifinals that effectively submarined their chances of further advancement.

In non-garbage-time minutes, the Warriors have outscored opponents by more than seven points per 100 possessions in Steph/Jimmy/Draymond floor time, by more than 10 points-per-100 when Curry and Green play without Butler or when Butler and Green play without Curry, and by more than nine points-per-100 when Jimmy flies solo without the Warriors’ longtime cornerstones. Butler’s presence unlocked Curry and elevated the Warriors; his absence, combined with myriad other injuries and inconsistencies, left Golden State relatively rudderless.
